actions: Read sanitized root manifest and evaluation role-local config at one frozen main SHA with two presemantic SHA-only ref readbacks.
Read only evaluation LATEST/checkpoint and attempted own sanitized feedback (404).
Read three public primary/preprint sources on heavy-tailed LLM scheduling and conditional sequential testing.
Ran worker-local synthetic stress comparing random statistical order to prelaunch predicted-short-first order under predictor error.
Constructed a marginal-null but predictor-conditional sign-asymmetry counterexample and quantified false-commit inflation.
Persisted checkpoint and advanced role-local LATEST with CAS/readback discipline.

outputs.new_rule: Prelaunch provenance is necessary for predictability but insufficient for statistical safety: any covariate used to choose statistical inclusion/reveal order must be covered by the conditional null or explicitly conditioned/stratified in inference.
outputs.latency_result: Under q=0.75 independent signs, synthetic predicted-short-first reduced q95 wall by about 30-76% across predictor-quality cells while unresolved rate stayed about 8-9%.
outputs.validity_result: Under a marginally fair null with sign-latency dependence, predictor-sorted false commits rose from about 3.8% random-order to 6.6-17.6% for mild beta=0.25 and 10.5-45.1% for beta=0.5 across tested predictor quality.

termination: runtime checkpoint with nonempty frontier; not global completion
exact_next_action: Simulate a two-layer scheduler with covariate-blind random statistical reveal order and predictor-driven physical scheduling inside windows W in {16,32,64}; compare q95 wall and occupancy to fixed launch and predictor-sorted statistical order, and verify false-commit control under the same marginal-null sign-latency counterexample.
